acceptance_test_matrix: DROP_NEW sustained-overrun semantic coverage verifies incoming records are dropped after edge capacity is exceeded, already accepted queued records remain observable, and no overflow spill file is created.
DROP_OLD sustained-overrun semantic coverage verifies oldest queued records are evicted under pressure, newest accepted records drain in expected order, and queue capacity invariants hold.
BLOCK sustained-overrun semantic coverage verifies producer admission blocks under capacity pressure, unblocks when the consumer drains, does not busy-spin, and does not lose accepted records.

OVERFLOW_TO_DISK sustained-overrun semantic coverage verifies excess accepted records spill through MmapJournal-backed storage, drain back correctly after in-memory records, and spill file contents are read back and asserted during drain.

Edge-level policy hot-swap coverage verifies an active edge can switch policies without graph rebuild, record corruption, duplicate acceptance, stale policy use, or behavior changes on unrelated edges.
R-002 snapshot/journal prerequisite coverage verifies overflow spill persistence cannot proceed unless the durability prerequisite is present and compatible.
Stale or invalid spill lifecycle coverage verifies stale spill files and invalid spill state are rejected or recovered without silent data acceptance.
Invariant or CRC-equivalent failure coverage verifies corrupted, truncated, or invariant-violating journal state is detected and fails closed.

Failure and partial acceptance coverage verifies partial spill write, partial drain, and interrupted overflow handling do not lose, duplicate, or reorder accepted records outside declared policy semantics.
Configured QA gate coverage verifies ./qa/smoke.sh, ./qa/regression.sh, ./gradlew jmhSmokeCheck, and the allocation gate remain green.
assumptions: GraphPartitionRunner.Builder is the intended public entry point for default and per-edge backpressure policy configuration and edge-level hot-swap.
BackpressurePolicy is a public enum with exactly DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, and OVERFLOW_TO_DISK.
Existing runtime edge queues can be extended without changing graph definition semantics outside the new policy selector.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must reuse existing MmapJournal or equivalent lvc-standard journal machinery from dag-framework-lvc and must not introduce a bespoke spill serialization format.

R-006 is dependency-gated on the R-002 snapshot or journal durability prerequisite; if that prerequisite is absent or incompatible, implementation must pause for repair or replan instead of bypassing it.
Sustained-overrun tests and fixtures can be authored under tests/ and qa/fixtures/ before implementation.
Allocation gate coverage is represented by existing smoke, regression, and jmhSmokeCheck commands unless the repository exposes a more specific allocation command during implementation.

acceptance_test_matrix: DROP_NEW sustained-overrun semantic coverage verifies incoming records are dropped after edge capacity is exceeded, already accepted queued records remain observable, and no overflow spill file is created.
DROP_OLD sustained-overrun semantic coverage verifies oldest queued records are evicted under pressure, newest accepted records drain in expected order, and queue capacity invariants hold.
BLOCK sustained-overrun semantic coverage verifies producer admission blocks under capacity pressure, unblocks when the consumer drains, does not busy-spin, and does not lose accepted records.

OVERFLOW_TO_DISK sustained-overrun semantic coverage verifies excess accepted records spill through MmapJournal-backed storage, drain back correctly after in-memory records, and spill file contents are read back and asserted during drain.

Edge-level policy hot-swap coverage verifies an active edge can switch policies without graph rebuild, record corruption, duplicate acceptance, stale policy use, or behavior changes on unrelated edges.
R-002 prerequisite coverage verifies overflow spill persistence cannot proceed unless the snapshot or journal durability prerequisite is confirmed.
Stale or invalid spill lifecycle coverage verifies stale spill files and invalid spill state are rejected or recovered without silent data acceptance.
Invariant or CRC-equivalent failure coverage verifies corrupted, truncated, or invariant-violating journal state is detected and fails closed.

Failure and partial acceptance coverage verifies partial spill write, partial drain, and interrupted overflow handling do not lose, duplicate, or reorder accepted records outside declared policy semantics.
Configured QA gate coverage verifies ./qa/smoke.sh, ./qa/regression.sh, ./gradlew jmhSmokeCheck, and the allocation gate remain green.
assumptions: GraphPartitionRunner.Builder is the intended public entry point for default and per-edge backpressure policy configuration and edge-level hot-swap.
BackpressurePolicy is a first-class public enum rather than string-based configuration.
Existing runtime edge queues can be extended without changing graph definition semantics outside the new policy selector.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must reuse existing MmapJournal or equivalent lvc-standard journal machinery from dag-framework-lvc and must not introduce a bespoke spill serialization format.

R-006 is dependency-gated on the R-002 snapshot or journal durability prerequisite; the design slice must verify that prerequisite is complete or explicitly block implementation until it is satisfied.
Sustained-overrun tests and fixtures can be authored under tests/ and qa/fixtures/ before implementation.
Allocation gate coverage is represented by existing smoke, regression, and jmhSmokeCheck commands unless the repository exposes a more specific allocation command during implementation.

acceptance_tests: DROP_NEW sustained overrun rejects new records when edge capacity is exceeded and preserves already queued records for drain.
DROP_OLD sustained overrun evicts oldest queued records, admits newer records, and drains in expected order while preserving capacity invariants.
BLOCK sustained overrun blocks producer admission until capacity is available, unblocks on consumer drain, avoids busy-spin, and does not drop accepted records.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK sustained overrun spills excess accepted records through MmapJournal-backed storage, drains memory plus spill in FIFO order, and verifies spill file readback.
Edge-level hot-swap changes the selected edge policy at runtime for subsequent admissions without graph rebuild and without affecting other edges.
R-002 snapshot or journal durability prerequisite is verified before spill persistence implementation proceeds.
Stale or invalid spill state is detected before unsafe reuse and is rejected or recovered according to existing journal semantics.
Invariant or CRC-equivalent journal failure, including corrupt or truncated spill state, is detected and fails closed.
Partial spill write, partial drain, and interrupted overflow handling do not silently lose, duplicate, or reorder accepted records outside declared policy semantics.
./qa/smoke.sh, ./qa/regression.sh, ./gradlew jmhSmokeCheck, and the allocation gate pass.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Policy selection is evaluated at edge admission through edge-scoped state that is safely visible to concurrent producers and consumers. DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD must preserve queue invariants under sustained overrun. BLOCK must wait without busy-spin and without cross-partition or unrelated-edge propagation. OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must serialize spill and drain transitions so accepted records are neither lost, duplicated, nor reordered outside the selected policy semantics during hot-swap.
forbidden_alternatives: String-based policy names without a BackpressurePolicy enum.
Global-only runner policy that cannot be configured per edge.
Custom spill serialization separate from existing MmapJournal or lvc-standard journal machinery.
Priority queues, weighted shedding, source-level priority dropping, or conflation.
Blocking behavior that stalls unrelated partitions or unrelated edges.
Policy hot-swap requiring graph rebuild or process restart.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK implementation that bypasses or assumes the R-002 durability prerequisite.
Tests that cover only nominal single-record overflow rather than sustained overrun.
hard_constraints: Expose only DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, and OVERFLOW_TO_DISK; do not add custom backpressure policies.
Do not add priority-based shedding or source-side conflation behavior.
Do not add cross-partition backpressure propagation.
Reuse MmapJournal or equivalent lvc-standard machinery instead of inventing a new spill file format.
Confirm the R-002 snapshot or journal durability prerequisite before implementing OVERFLOW_TO_DISK persistence behavior.
Keep allocation gate, ./gradlew jmhSmokeCheck, ./qa/smoke.sh, and ./qa/regression.sh green.
QA author and QA verify slices may write only tests/ and qa/fixtures/.
Implementer slices must not write tests/ or qa/fixtures/.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: dag-framework-api owns public enum and builder-facing configuration contracts; runtime-core owns edge queue admission, drop/block semantics, hot-swap behavior, overflow admission, and drain ordering; dag-framework-lvc owns reusable MmapJournal-backed spill persistence integration; tests/ and qa/fixtures/ own failing acceptance tests and QA fixtures; repo-memory/ owns verification of the R-002 prerequisite and any roadmap decision notes.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: OVERFLOW_TO_DISK persists overflow records through existing MmapJournal/EventJournal machinery only after the R-002 snapshot or journal durability prerequisite is confirmed. It drains in-memory records and spilled records in declared edge order, asserts spill readback during drain, rejects or recovers stale and invalid spill state according to existing journal semantics, fails closed on invariant or CRC-equivalent journal failure, and handles partial spill/write/drain failure without silently accepting corrupt, lost, duplicated, or reordered records.
